raw_pool.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
raw_pool.snippet: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation , and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO. And then… Huang was back. In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation. raw_pool.title: Apple to Release Four (RED) Products by Next Week
raw_pool.snippet: Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman this week reported that Apple plans to release (PRODUCT)RED versions of the existing AirPods Max 2 and HomePod mini 2 on or around Tuesday, December 1, which is World AIDS Day. The new color will likely be the only change. AirPods Max 2 and HomePod mini 2 in (PRODUCT)RED (concept) Gurman said the (PRODUCT)RED version of the HomePod mini 2 will have a red mesh exterior, and he said the special-edition AirPods Max 2 will have a silver finish, white ear cushions, a white headband, and a red Digital Crown. AirPods Max 2 launched in March for $549 , while the HomePod mini 2 arrived last month for $149 . In a follow-up social media post , Gurman revealed that Apple is planning to release an additional two accessories in the (PRODUCT)RED color as part of this launch: a Wrist Strap for AirPods Pro and a Sport Band for the Apple Watch. Wrist Strap and Apple Watch Sport Band in (PRODUCT)RED (concept) Since 2006, Apple has partnered with the (RED) brand to raise money for The Global Fund , an organization that aims to combat diseases such as HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria in Africa. Through this partnership, Apple had long offered a (PRODUCT)RED option for some products, but the color has not been offered for a while now . (RED) was co-founded by U2 singer Bono, and Apple's partnership with the brand goes back to the Steve Jobs days. Apple continues to support The Global Fund through its annual Apple Pay donation program, which raised $3 million last year . Apple offered a variety of iPod, iPhone, and Apple Watch models in (PRODUCT)RED over the years, with some of the most recent products available in the color being the iPhone SE 3, iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Plus, and Apple Watch Series 9. A variety of iPhone cases, Apple Watch bands, and other accessories also came in the color. raw_pool.title: iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18 Rumored to Feature Thicker Cameras
raw_pool.snippet: The iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18 will feature noticeably thicker camera bumps, according to Engadget . Engadget says it has seen computer-aided design (CAD) files showing the ‌iPhone Air‌ 2 with two rear cameras positioned side-by-side. The camera plateau reportedly measures 3.8mm thick, up from 3.45mm on the current model, while the device's body remains 5.6mm thick. The layout essentially resembles dummy models shared by Sonny Dickson last week. Those mockups position both cameras horizontally toward the left of the plateau, with the flash and microphone continuing to be placed on the right. Multiple previous reports have suggested that Apple will add an Ultra Wide camera, with analyst Jeff Pu predicting a 48-megapixel sensor . Other anticipated upgrades include the A20 Pro chip, Apple's C2 modem, an N2 wireless networking chip, and longer battery life . Pu expects the device to retain its 6.5-inch display , 12GB of RAM, and 18-megapixel Center Stage front camera. The same CAD files also reportedly depict the standard ‌iPhone 18‌, showing an unchanged appearance over the iPhone 17 . Its camera housing also increases from 3.45mm to 3.8mm. Engadget says the files came from a supply chain source who previously shared accurate details about ‌iPhone 17‌ and iPhone 18 Pro colors. The ‌iPhone Air‌ 2 and ‌iPhone 18‌ are expected to launch in early 2027 alongside the iPhone 18e. raw_pool.title: Things 3.25 for Mac Gains Touch Gestures
raw_pool.snippet: Cultured Code today released Things 3.25 for Mac, bringing full optimization for the PROLED MacBook Pro to its task management app. Since the touchscreen MacBook Pro launched, all Mac apps feature basic touch input, with taps performing the equivalent of mouse clicks. Things already worked with that default behavior, but Cultured Code says version 3.25 fully optimizes the app for touch with additional gestures, improved dragging, and larger controls. A rightward swipe on a to-do opens the scheduling dialog, while a leftward swipe selects or deselects it. Users can also select several items by moving two fingers up or down through a list. To open a to-do, users can tap it to select it and tap again to expand it, or double-tap. Cultured Code says dragging to-dos and headings is smoother and more responsive, whether moving one item or a group. Holding a finger on an item in a selection picks up the whole group, rather than only that item. The update also improves how dragging works when some selected items are outside the visible area of the list. Custom menus and date pickers adapt to the input method, showing more spacious rows and larger touch targets when opened with a finger. Buttons elsewhere in the app also have larger tap targets. Other changes make it easier to resize the sidebar by touch and rearrange checklist entries within a to-do. Users can cancel either a to-do or an individual checklist entry by pressing and holding its checkbox. The release also includes smaller adjustments to touch interactions and interface polish throughout the app. Things 3.25 for Mac is available now. raw_pool.snippet: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO , following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith's radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would "end up on his feet." "You know the expression, anybody can be replaced," Trump said, floating Apple's ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn't take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he'd welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia's own board wasn't ready to do so.
